newsitem.title: USA: Cunanan resting place unknown, mother grieves.
newsitem.headline: Cunanan resting place unknown, mother grieves.

text.p: The final resting place of the accused spree killer whose victims allegedly included Italian fashion designer Gianni Versace was a mystery on Monday.
In death as in life, Andrew Cunanan remained elusive.

A Miami undertaker was to have cremated him and sent his ashes to a suburban San Diego funeral home, but that funeral parlour denied the ashes had arrived and insisted it would not hold a service for or bury him.
Meawhile, there were unconfirmed reports that a local church had held some sort of memorial service for Cunanan, who until his suicide last week was the nation's most wanted man.
His family remained in hiding, although his mother issued a statement through her lawyer expressing sorrow.

The statement from MaryAnn Cunanan, read to reporters by lawyer Connie Viado, said: "Six men have lost their lives and now the families must pick up the pieces. To those families I share in your sorrow. I grieve with you for the tragic loss of your loved ones.
"I loved my son Andrew deeply and I hope and pray that he is in peace. His journey has ended and now we are left to walk without him."
Cunanan is believed to have killed five men as well as taking his own life.
Genn Abbey Memorial Park in the San Diego suburb of Bonita said it had arranged for Cunanan's body to be cremated, but it denied receiving his ashes or planning a funeral.

It said it had arranged for a Miami funeral home to cremate Cunanan's body after he committed suicide last Wednesday while an army of police was searching for him in south Florida and across the country.
An employee at the funeral home said it had not yet received the ashes and added that there had been some sort of memorial service for him at St. Rita's Church.
But a church employee could not confirm that, and church officials were not available for comment.
Cunanan's body was released to a Miami funeral home on Saturday, three days after he shot himself on being discovered on a houseboat.
"The family asked that we keep things as quiet as possible," a spokesman for the Miami funeral home told Reuters.
Cunanan is accused of gunning down Versace on the steps of the designer's oceanfront mansion on July 15.
Police found Cunanan's body on Wednesday after storming a houseboat about two miles (3.2 km) north of Versace's home.
The medical examiner's office would say only that Cunanan died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

They would not say whether he was already dead when police stormed the houseboat or whether he carried the HIV virus. There have been reports that Cunanan's alleged killing spree was triggered by the discovery that he carried the virus that causes AIDS.
